niche_preference_profile: Prefers polished, high-intent interfaces with strong hierarchy, clear task framing, explicit navigation, and composed editorial structure. They repeatedly favor premium-feeling layouts with restrained copy, fewer but larger grouped sections, strong CTA emphasis, clear state visibility, and visually grounded full-screen compositions rather than isolated or generic components. They often like serious, assertive, high-contrast treatments in task-critical or financial contexts, but also value calm spacing, cohesion, and reduced clutter.

criteria.description: Prefers a clear top-to-bottom hierarchy with a prominent title, obvious grouping, and unmistakable emphasis on the primary content and action.
Prefers cleaner screens with fewer decorative elements, less repeated card chrome, and lower visual noise.
Prefers interfaces that feel editorial, intentional, premium, and composed rather than template-like or generic app screens.
Prefers content organized into coherent sections or modules with a readable staged flow rather than fragmented or mixed blocks.
Prefers explicit back/next controls, visible progression, and grounded navigation that makes the flow feel anchored and guided.
Prefers a highly visible, decisive primary action with strong contrast and clear priority over secondary actions.
Prefers screens that read as one unified experience rather than a collection of disconnected modules or floating components.
Prefers UI elements, especially modals, to sit within a visible surrounding screen context with app chrome, page framing, and layered realism.
Prefers shorter, more direct, less chatty copy that communicates efficiently without filler.
Prefers controls whose active states and interaction affordances are obvious, tactile, and easy to interpret.
Prefers even spacing, breathing room, and a disciplined vertical rhythm between major sections and controls.
Prefers a serious, composed, productivity- or finance-oriented tone, especially for operational or alert-driven screens.
Prefers stronger contrast on text, selected controls, and key actions so important elements stand out clearly.
Prefers screens that keep the main task dominant and avoid diluting attention with extra feature explanations or competing messages.
Prefers fewer, larger, more substantial modules instead of many small nested cards or repetitive utility blocks.
Prefers direct, plain, utilitarian labels and headings that improve scanability over branded, bureaucratic, or overly feature-led naming.
In alert contexts, prefers semantically urgent styling such as vivid warning colors, stronger caution signals, and commanding action treatment.
Prefers softer, rounded, contemporary buttons and controls, especially pill-like primary actions.
Prefers visible layering, depth, and surrounding supporting modules that make the interface feel like a complete product system.
